I've been working this land in Quzhou for over forty years. The North China Plain tells you what to grow — there's no arguing with it. Winter wheat into summer maize, that's the backbone of life here, same rotation I've run since I was young. I have about 12 mu, and I'll keep all of it in the wheat-corn double-crop system. At my age I'm not going to start chasing cotton or vegetables at scale — too much hand labor, and my knees aren't what they were.

I'll plant improved wheat this season, probably Jimai 22 or whatever the county agricultural bureau is recommending locally this year — I check in with them. I've stopped using old landraces; the yield gap is too big. Same logic for summer maize — I'll go with a hybrid, likely Zhengdan 958 or similar. I've used it for years, I know how it behaves on my soil.

On fertilizer, I know the research coming out of the Quzhou Experimental Station well. I've watched neighbors over-apply nitrogen their whole lives and get yield plateaus and more aphids. I'll base-apply compound fertilizer and topdress nitrogen at jointing for wheat — total around 14 kg N per mu. For maize I go a bit heavier on nitrogen given the yield target, around 16 kg, mostly as urea sidedressed at V6.

Irrigation is where I'm most careful now. Hebei has been squeezing groundwater quotas for years, and rightly so — I've seen the water table drop in my lifetime. For wheat I'll do three irrigations: once around sowing if soil moisture is short, once at jointing, once at grain-filling. I skip the overwintering irrigation unless we get no snow. For maize I'll rely on July-August rains and only pump if it looks like tasseling stress — maybe once or twice.

For tillage, I rotary-till the wheat seedbed in October. After wheat harvest in June I no-till the maize directly into the stubble — saves fuel, saves time, and I've found my maize yields are just as good. My son-in-law helps with the tractor work.

Pest management is straightforward: herbicide pass early in wheat, one fungicide/aphid spray around heading. Maize gets a corn borer treatment if the pressure is bad, otherwise I leave it.

I'm targeting 450 kg/mu on wheat and 550 kg/mu on maize. These are honest numbers, not wishful ones.
